about: Use-case evaluation corpus. Expected results were written BEFORE running any build on these documents, from dataset annotations (CUAD, FUNSD, CORU, INV-CDIP, Voxel51), from the generator's data (synthetic documents), or by an AI reading the original files (UN documents, IRS forms, Wikipedia). Files are not in the repository; bench/usecases/README.md lists where each comes from. Groups keep translations and near-duplicates in the same split. Reserved documents are evaluated only with --split reserved, which is logged. A third split, 'fresh' (10 documents), was added after the reserved evaluation, to check on unseen documents the fixes the reserved run prompted; its expectations were written before any build was run on it. Date expectations accept the ISO form of the same date (added uniformly to every question after the first runs; it changes scoring, never outcomes). A fourth split, 'fresh2' (15 genuine documents), was added on 2026-10-25 for an independent check of missing-information handling. Its expectations, including unanswerable questions marked 'absent_subject' (the document never mentions what is asked) or 'present_subject' (it mentions the subject but not the asked value), were written before any build was run on these files. A fifth split, 'fresh3' (11 genuine documents), was added on 2026-10-25 to evaluate whether answers are connected to what was asked (sender vs recipient, document date vs event date, subtotal vs total, tax mentioned vs tax amount). Answerable questions carry a 'category'. Expectations were written before any build was run on these files.
gaps: Genuine Arabic forms, certificates, invoices and contracts with an open licence: none found. Synthetic stand-ins are used and labelled.
Arabic-only genuine receipts: CORU receipts are mostly bilingual; treated as mixed.
